Your inbox mixes your to-do list with everyone else's, sorted by whoever wrote last.

Inbox Zero is a free, open-source email assistant built by one developer. It solves a few different problems:
- blocks cold email
- drafts replies in your voice
- tracks who owes a reply, in both directions
- files your attachments

The reply tracker is the one worth the setup. It splits the threads where you're the holdup from the ones where you're waiting on someone else.

Then connect Claude and tell it how to handle incoming mail in plain language. Claude's replies stay as drafts until you send them, and your email stays in Gmail or Outlook.

One honest note: anything you connect to your email deserves a proper look at what it can access before you switch it on.

Google just open-sourced Mantis: a set of security skills that turns your coding agent into a full review team.

Don't just trust the code your AI hands back. Mantis maps your code and builds a threat model. Then it hunts weak spots, drops the duplicates, and tries to prove each bug is real.

When a bug is real, it can write a patch, rerun the attack, and rank the risk that's left. Your developer gets the proof and the fix in one report.

The important part: run it only inside an isolated, locked-down setup. Mantis can write and run unstable code, and every finding still needs a security expert to check it.
